## Overview

**Core question:** When `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering` drives a long randomized sequence of begin/end rendering instances that mix suspend/resume chains, secondary command buffers, multiple graphics pipeline shapes (vertex-fragment, geometry, tessellation, multiview, layered, attachment-clear), occlusion queries, and randomized render areas and load ops, does the implementation keep the color image and query results consistent with the spec?

- This page covers the `random` test family implemented in [vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp).
- The family is registered under `renderpasses.dynamic_rendering.primary_cmd_buff.random` by [vktRenderPassTests.cpp#L8532](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassTests.cpp#L8532), and the `random` group itself is created by [createDynamicRenderingRandomTests](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L1094-L1116).
- Unlike most other dynamic-rendering families, `random` is attached only under the `primary_cmd_buff` intermediate node and only when secondary command buffers are not globally mandated by the parent group parameters. It is excluded from Vulkan SC builds.
- Each test case seeds a deterministic pseudo-random sequence and runs 50 rendering iterations against a 4-layer color image. The test builds a host-side reference image pixel by pixel from the same random draws, then compares the device output against that reference and checks occlusion query results.
- 800 test case leaves are generated by the cross product of three feature flags (`geometry`, `tessellation`, `multiview`) and 100 seeds.

## Background Knowledge

- **Dynamic rendering instead of render passes.** `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering` (promoted to Vulkan 1.3) lets an application draw without creating a `VkRenderPass` or `VkFramebuffer`. The application calls `vkCmdBeginRendering`/`vkCmdEndRendering` and describes attachments inline through `VkRenderingInfo` and `VkRenderingAttachmentInfo`. Graphics pipelines are made compatible with this path by passing a `VkPipelineRenderingCreateInfo` chain at pipeline creation instead of a render pass handle. This page assumes familiarity with that begin/end structure; the test exists to exercise it under randomized, interleaved conditions rather than to introduce it.
- **Suspended and resumed render pass instances.** A render pass instance can set `VK_RENDERING_SUSPENDING_BIT_KHR`, and a later instance can set `VK_RENDERING_RESUMING_BIT_KHR` to continue it. The spec requires the contents of `VkRenderingInfo` to match between the suspended and resuming instances (except for the suspend/resume and secondary-command-buffer flag bits), and forbids any action, synchronization, or other render pass instance between them. The resumed instance uses a new command buffer. This constraint is central to the test: once a sequence is suspended, the next iteration cannot randomize new rendering parameters and must keep the same view mask and layer count.
- **Multiview through `viewMask`.** Under dynamic rendering, multiview is enabled by a nonzero `viewMask` in `VkRenderingInfo`. Each set bit names an active view, and `gl_ViewIndex` in the shader reports which view a fragment belongs to. The test uses a fixed view mask of `0xb` (binary `1011`), which activates layers 0, 1, and 3.
- **Layered rendering via `gl_Layer`.** A geometry shader can write `gl_Layer` to direct a primitive to a specific array layer of the color attachment. The test also exercises `vkCmdClearAttachments` with a `VkClearRect` that targets a chosen layer and layer count.

## Registration Hierarchy

```text
renderpasses.dynamic_rendering.primary_cmd_buff.random
├── seed0
├── seed0_geometry
├── seed0_geometry_multiview
├── seed0_geometry_tessellation
├── seed0_geometry_tessellation_multiview
├── seed0_multiview
├── seed0_tessellation
├── seed0_tessellation_multiview
└── seed99_tessellation_multiview
```

The `random` test family is created by [createDynamicRenderingRandomTests](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L1094-L1116) and attached only under `primary_cmd_buff` at [vktRenderPassTests.cpp#L8532](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassTests.cpp#L8532). Each seed produces 8 leaves: one bare leaf, one per single feature suffix, three pairwise suffixes, and one triple suffix. Test names are built by [addDynamicRenderingTest](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L1083-L1090) as `seed{N}{_geometry}{_tessellation}{_multiview}`. The full leaf count is 100 seeds times 8 flag combinations equals 800 test cases.

## Behavior Parameters

The primary behavioral axis is the feature-flag suffix encoded in the test case name. Each suffix enables a distinct set of pipeline types that the random sequence can select, and therefore a distinct set of rendering paths that must stay consistent with the reference image.

### Bare `seed{N}`: vertex-fragment and attachment-clear only

The minimum case. Only `PIPELINE_TYPE_VERTEX_FRAGMENT` and `PIPELINE_TYPE_ATTACHMENT_CLEAR` are valid, so every iteration either draws a triangle-strip quad through the basic vertex-fragment pipeline or clears a rectangular region of one layer via `vkCmdClearAttachments`. This is the baseline against which the feature-enabled variants add complexity. The basic pipeline draws into layer 0 only.

### `_geometry`: adds geometry-shader and layered pipelines

Enabling geometry adds two pipeline types. `PIPELINE_TYPE_VERTEX_GEOM_FRAGMENT` draws a single point that a geometry shader expands into a quad. `PIPELINE_TYPE_VERTEX_GEOM_FRAGMENT_LAYER` uses a vertex shader that applies the push-constant scale and offset, then a geometry shader writes `gl_Layer` from the push constant to direct the primitive to a randomly chosen layer. Because layered pipelines render to all four layers when clearing and to one chosen layer when drawing, the active-layer mask tracked by the reference image differs from the basic case.

### `_tessellation`: adds a tessellated quad pipeline

Enabling tessellation adds `PIPELINE_TYPE_VERTEX_TESS_FRAGMENT`. The vertex shader runs as in the basic case; a tessellation control shader sets all inner and outer levels to 2.0 and passes positions through; the evaluation shader interpolates the four patch corners with a quad `gl_TessCoord`. The result is a quad covering the same area as the triangle-strip version, so tessellation exercises a different primitive-generation path without changing the expected image geometry.

### `_multiview`: adds a multiview pipeline

Enabling multiview adds `PIPELINE_TYPE_VERTEX_FRAGMENT_MULTIVIEW`. This pipeline is created with view mask `0xb`, so one draw renders to layers 0, 1, and 3 simultaneously. The fragment shader overwrites the blue channel with `0.15 * gl_ViewIndex`, which makes each view's contribution distinguishable in the reference image. Multiview is the only pipeline type whose view mask cannot change across a suspend/resume boundary, so the random sequence has a special rule to keep it selected across that boundary.

### Combinations: `_geometry_tessellation`, `_geometry_multiview`, `_tessellation_multiview`, `_geometry_tessellation_multiview`

Each combination simply enables the union of the corresponding pipeline types and requires the union of the corresponding features. The random sequence selects among all enabled pipelines on every iteration, subject to the suspend/resume consistency constraints. There is no separate code path per combination; the enabled set is computed once from the feature flags at [validPipelines construction](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L429-L438).

## Shader Analysis

The shaders are not the tested behavior. They exist to produce a known, simple output so that host-side reference tracking and pixel comparison can detect dynamic-rendering state-handling bugs. The fragment shader writes the push-constant color with one of two blue-channel modes: zero for non-multiview pipelines, or `0.15 * gl_ViewIndex` for multiview. Because shader output is trivial and identical across all 800 cases modulo the blue-channel mode, no representative shader walkthrough is included.

## Runtime Execution and Result Checking

Each test case runs 50 iterations in a single primary command buffer (or a chain of primary command buffers when suspend/resume occurs). The host drives the entire sequence deterministically from the seeded `de::Random` instance.

Per-iteration randomized choices, drawn at [the main loop](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L440-L780):

- **Pipeline type.** Selected from the valid pipeline mask, with extra filtering during a resume to preserve the view mask and layer count of the suspended instance. See [pipeline selection](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L492-L523).
- **Secondary command buffer.** Chosen with probability 1/5. When used, the draw is recorded in a secondary command buffer with `VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_USAGE_RENDER_PASS_CONTINUE_BIT` and a `VkCommandBufferInheritanceRenderingInfoKHR` that mirrors the render instance's flags, view mask, and format. The pipeline bind moves into the secondary buffer.
- **Bind timing.** A coin flip decides whether the pipeline is bound before or after `vkCmdBeginRendering`. Secondary-command-buffer iterations always bind after, because the bind must live in the same buffer as the draw.
- **Render area, clear color, load op.** Re-randomized only when not resuming. The render area is a randomly placed, even-sized sub-rectangle of the 256x256 image. The load op is randomly `CLEAR` or `LOAD`.
- **Suspend.** Chosen with probability 1/5 and suppressed on the last iteration. When suspended, the next iteration must resume with identical `VkRenderingInfo` contents, uses a new primary command buffer, and shrinks the quad so the previously drawn quad stays visible underneath.
- **Occlusion query.** A coin flip, disabled for attachment-clear iterations. Multiview iterations advance the query index by 3 (one per active view); others advance by 1.
- **Push-constant color and layer.** A random RGB color and, for layered pipelines, a random layer index.

Reference image tracking happens inline with command recording. For each iteration the host updates a per-layer software image: it applies the clear color to the active layers when the load op is `CLEAR` and the instance is not resuming, then writes the quad color to the active layers inside the drawn rectangle. The multiview pipeline's per-view blue channel and the attachment-clear path's layer targeting are both accounted for in this tracking.

After the loop:

- A pipeline barrier with `VK_ACCESS_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT` on both sides is inserted after each non-suspending iteration to separate consecutive render instances.
- Query results are copied back with `vkCmdCopyQueryPoolResults` using `VK_QUERY_RESULT_WAIT_BIT`.
- The color image is copied to a host-visible buffer, one copy per layer.
- The command buffer chain is submitted behind a fence and waited on.

Final checks, at [verification](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L816-L851):

- Each of the 4 layers is compared against its reference image using `tcu::floatThresholdCompare` with a per-channel threshold of `0.02f`. Any mismatch fails the case.
- Occlusion query results are scanned. Every recorded query must sum to a nonzero sample count; a zero sum fails the case with "Expected nonzero occlusion query results."

## Failure Meaning

### Failure Cause Mapping

| If this behavior parameter value fails | Possible failure cause(s) |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Any `seed{N}` leaf | Dynamic-rendering state tracking: incorrect suspend/resume `VkRenderingInfo` matching, broken render-area or load-op handling, wrong layer targeting, or occlusion query accounting that reports zero samples for visible geometry |
| Any `_geometry` leaf | Additionally: geometry-shader expansion or `gl_Layer` routing that writes to the wrong layer |
| Any `_tessellation` leaf | Additionally: tessellation coordinate interpolation that moves the quad off the expected rectangle |
| Any `_multiview` leaf | Additionally: multiview view-mask handling that renders to the wrong views or misreports `gl_ViewIndex` |
| Any `_geometry_tessellation`, `_geometry_multiview`, `_tessellation_multiview`, or `_geometry_tessellation_multiview` leaf | A combination of the above, or an interaction defect that only appears when multiple optional pipeline types are valid simultaneously |

### Cause Analysis

#### Dynamic-rendering state tracking failures

**Possible failure symptoms:** A layer's rendered image differs from the host-tracked reference beyond the `0.02f` threshold, or an occlusion query returns zero for a draw that should have produced visible samples.

**Possible implementation causes:** The driver or command buffer recording layer mishandles one of the randomized interleavings. Likely candidates include incorrect suspend/resume matching (for example, mutating `VkRenderingInfo` contents across the boundary, or inserting a forbidden command between suspend and resume), wrong render-area clipping, mishandling `VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_LOAD` versus `VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_CLEAR` across consecutive instances, or losing track of which layers a given pipeline type targets. Source-level investigation is needed to pin a specific failure to one of these; the test design deliberately entangles them so that a single failed seed narrows the reproduction to a short deterministic sequence.

#### Geometry-shader layer routing failures

**Possible failure symptoms:** Only the `_geometry` and layered variants mismatch, and the mismatch is confined to layers other than layer 0, or to the wrong single layer when `PIPELINE_TYPE_VERTEX_GEOM_FRAGMENT_LAYER` was selected.

**Possible implementation causes:** The geometry shader writes `gl_Layer` from a push constant, so a driver bug that ignores or misroutes `gl_Layer` would direct the quad to the wrong layer. A bug in geometry-shader point-to-quad expansion would shrink or distort the quad. These are shader-stage and fixed-function layer-routing defects specific to the geometry path.

#### Tessellation interpolation failures

**Possible failure symptoms:** Only the `_tessellation` variants mismatch, and the mismatch follows the quad outline (edges or corners displaced) rather than a full-layer color shift.

**Possible implementation causes:** The tessellation evaluation shader bilinearly interpolates four patch corners using `gl_TessCoord`. A driver or compiler bug that miscomputes tessellation coordinates, or that lowers the quad patch incorrectly, would move the interpolated position and thus the quad boundary. The fixed tessellation levels (all 2.0) make the expected geometry deterministic, so a displacement points directly at tessellation-coordinate handling.

#### Multiview view-mask failures

**Possible failure symptoms:** Only the `_multiview` variants mismatch, and the mismatch is on layers 0, 1, or 3 (the bits set in view mask `0xb`), or the per-view blue channel does not match `0.15 * view_index`.

**Possible implementation causes:** A driver that renders multiview draws to the wrong set of layers, or that supplies a wrong `gl_ViewIndex` to the fragment shader, would produce the observed pattern. Because the multiview pipeline is the only one whose view mask must not change across suspend/resume, a bug in preserving the view mask across that boundary would also surface here.

## Case Pruning

### Requirement-based pruning

- `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering` and the `dynamicRendering` feature are required for every case. See [checkSupport](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L880-L897).
- `VK_KHR_multiview` is required when `enableMultiview` is set.
- `DEVICE_CORE_FEATURE_GEOMETRY_SHADER` is required when `enableGeometry` is set.
- `DEVICE_CORE_FEATURE_TESSELLATION_SHADER` is required when `enableTessellation` is set.
- The entire `random` family is registered only under `primary_cmd_buff` and only when the parent group does not mandate secondary command buffers, so it is absent from `partial_secondary_cmd_buff` and `complete_secondary_cmd_buff`. See [registration gate](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktRenderPassTests.cpp#L8529-L8540).

### Design-based pruning

- The last iteration never suspends, so a suspended sequence always has a resuming partner within the 50-iteration run. See [suspend suppression](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L529).
- Attachment-clear iterations never use occlusion queries, because `vkCmdClearAttachments` is not a draw and would not produce meaningful occlusion samples. See [query gating](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L525).
- The render area is forced to an even size so the margin around the drawn quad stays symmetrical, which keeps the reference image computation exact. See [even-size masking](../../../modules/vulkan/renderpass/vktDynamicRenderingRandomTests.cpp#L481-L484).

## Key Takeaways

- The test is a randomized stress harness for dynamic rendering state handling, not a shader test. Its value comes from 50-iteration sequences that interleave suspend/resume, secondary command buffers, and six pipeline types in varied but deterministic order.
- The host builds the reference image from the same `de::Random` stream that drives the device, so any divergence between device behavior and the spec-derived expectation shows up as a per-pixel mismatch at a reproducible seed.
- Suspend/resume is the most constrained path: the resuming instance must match the suspended instance's `VkRenderingInfo` exactly (modulo flags), must use a new command buffer, and must preserve the multiview view mask if the suspended instance was multiview.
- A zero occlusion-query result for a recorded draw is treated as a failure independent of the image comparison, giving the test a second, independent signal for draws that should have passed the depth/stencil test.
- Feature-flag suffixes do not create new code paths; they expand the set of valid pipelines the random sequence can select and the set of device features the case requires.
